description: Validated test tasks for V3 Agentic Harness evaluation. Tasks are organized by complexity level with clear success criteria.

tasks.description: Create a simple hello world function in Rust that returns the string 'Hello, World!' when called. The function should be named 'hello_world', take no parameters, and return a &'static str.
success_criteria: Function named 'hello_world' exists and compiles without errors
Function returns exactly the string 'Hello, World!'
Function has proper Rust documentation comment
Code follows Rust naming conventions

tasks.description: Create a recursive Rust function named 'fibonacci' that calculates the nth Fibonacci number. The function should take a u32 parameter 'n' and return a u64. For n=0 return 0, for n=1 return 1, for n>1 return fib(n-1) + fib(n-2).
success_criteria: Function named 'fibonacci' exists and compiles without errors
Function returns correct values: fibonacci(0)=0, fibonacci(1)=1, fibonacci(10)=55
Function handles edge cases correctly (n=0, n=1)
Function has proper documentation

tasks.description: Write unit tests for an existing 'add' function that takes two i32 parameters and returns their sum. Create at least 3 test cases: positive numbers, negative numbers, and zero. Use Rust's #[test] attribute.
success_criteria: At least 3 test functions exist with #[test] attribute
Tests cover positive numbers, negative numbers, and zero cases
All tests pass when run with 'cargo test'
Tests have descriptive names following Rust conventions

tasks.description: Write comprehensive documentation for a simple 'calculate_area' function that calculates the area of a rectangle. Include function purpose, parameters (width: f64, height: f64), return value (f64), example usage, and panics section if applicable.
success_criteria: Documentation includes function purpose description
Parameters are documented with types and descriptions
Return value is documented
At least one code example is provided in the documentation
Documentation compiles with rustdoc without warnings

tasks.description: Implement a UserValidator struct in Rust that validates user registration data. The validator should check: email format using regex, password strength (minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase, one lowercase, one number), and username length (3-20 characters, alphanumeric only). Return a Result<(), Vec<ValidationError>>.
success_criteria: UserValidator struct exists with validate method
Email validation uses proper regex pattern
Password validation checks all strength requirements
Username validation enforces length and character rules
Returns descriptive validation errors
All validation logic has unit tests

tasks.description: Refactor the following function to reduce cyclomatic complexity from 12 to under 5. The function processes order items and applies discounts. Extract helper functions, use early returns, and implement the strategy pattern for discount calculations. Maintain identical behavior.
success_criteria: Cyclomatic complexity reduced to under 5 per function
Original test suite still passes
Helper functions have single responsibility
Code is more readable and maintainable
No behavioral changes detected

tasks.description: Fix the memory leak in the ConnectionPool implementation. The issue is that connections are added to the pool but never removed when the pool is dropped. Implement proper Drop trait and ensure all connections are cleanly closed. Add tests that verify no memory is leaked.
success_criteria: Drop trait implemented for ConnectionPool
All connections are closed when pool is dropped
Memory usage does not grow after repeated pool creation/destruction
Tests verify proper cleanup behavior
No runtime errors or panics

tasks.description: Write integration tests for the TaskService that test the complete task lifecycle: creation, status updates, and completion. Tests should use a test database, handle async operations properly, and clean up after themselves. Cover both success and error paths.
success_criteria: Integration tests cover task creation, update, and completion
Tests use proper test database isolation
Async operations are properly awaited
Tests clean up created data after execution
Error cases are tested with appropriate assertions
Tests are properly documented

tasks.description: Implement a complete REST API endpoint for task management including: POST /tasks (create), GET /tasks/{id} (read), PUT /tasks/{id} (update), DELETE /tasks/{id} (delete). Include proper error handling, input validation, authentication middleware, and audit logging. Use Axum framework conventions.
success_criteria: All CRUD endpoints implemented and working
Input validation with descriptive error messages
Authentication middleware properly applied
Audit logging captures all operations
Proper HTTP status codes returned
API documentation generated
Integration tests cover all endpoints

tasks.description: Create a database migration system that supports: forward migrations, rollback migrations, version tracking, and dry-run mode. The system should read SQL files from a migrations directory, track which migrations have been applied, and support partial failure recovery.
success_criteria: Migration system can apply pending migrations in order
Rollback functionality works correctly
Migration state is persisted in database
Dry-run mode shows changes without applying
Partial failures leave database in consistent state
CLI interface for running migrations
Comprehensive test coverage

tasks.description: Implement a publish-subscribe event system with: typed events, multiple subscribers per event type, async event handlers, event replay from persistent storage, and dead letter queue for failed handlers. Ensure thread-safety and proper error propagation.
success_criteria: Events are strongly typed with compile-time safety
Multiple subscribers can register for same event type
Async handlers are properly scheduled and awaited
Events are persisted for replay capability
Failed handlers are tracked in dead letter queue
System is thread-safe for concurrent access
Comprehensive documentation and examples

tasks.description: Create a comprehensive test framework for the agent system that includes: mock LLM responses, simulated file system operations, time control for testing timeouts, assertion helpers for agent behavior, and test report generation. The framework should make writing agent tests simple and deterministic.
success_criteria: Mock LLM can return predetermined responses
File system mock supports all required operations
Time can be controlled for deterministic timeout testing
Custom assertion macros for agent behavior
Test reports are generated in multiple formats (JSON, HTML)
Framework is well-documented with examples
Existing tests can be migrated to use framework

simple.description: Baseline tasks to verify agent can complete simple, well-defined tasks

medium.description: Tasks with moderate complexity that require understanding context and making decisions

complex.description: Complex tasks that test agent limits and multi-step reasoning
